label: History
value: The Lion roared at men and animals to scare them away.
unit: The Lion spent his early life roaring at men and animals to scare them away before they could attack him, hiding his inner feelings of cowardice. Upon meeting Dorothy Gale, the Scarecrow, and the Tin Woodman, he admitted his fearfulness and decided to join their expedition to the Emerald City to request courage from the Great Oz. Along the road of yellow brick, he served as a faithful companion and guardian, though he was temporarily overcome by a poisonous poppy field until saved by the Queen of the Field Mice and her subjects. Upon reaching the Emerald City, he received a potion from Oz which he swallowed, believing it gave him genuine courage. Afterwards, he continued to accompany Dorothy and his friends on their subsequent trials.

label: History
value: Dorothy was raised on the Kansas prairies.
unit: Dorothy was raised on the Kansas prairies by her Aunt Em and Uncle Henry alongside her small black dog, Toto. A powerful cyclone struck her home, lifting the house into the air with Dorothy and Toto inside and carrying it to the Land of Oz. The house landed on and unintentionally killed the Wicked Witch of the East, granting Dorothy the magical Silver Shoes and a protective kiss from the Good Witch of the North. Seeking a way back to Kansas, Dorothy set off toward the Emerald City along the yellow brick road to consult the Great Oz. Along the journey, she befriended and rescued the Scarecrow, the Tin Woodman, and the Cowardly Lion, who joined her quest. Upon reaching the Emerald City, the Wizard tasked the companions with defeating the Wicked Witch of the West. While forced into servitude in the Witch's castle, Dorothy successfully melted the Wicked Witch with a bucket of water after her Silver Shoe was stolen. Returning to the Emerald City, she discovered the Wizard was a humbug unable to grant her request magically. Eventually, Dorothy traveled south to Glinda the Good Witch, who revealed the secret power of her Silver Shoes, allowing Dorothy to safely tap her heels and return home to Kansas with Toto.

The house landed on and unintentionally killed the Wicked Witch of the East, granting Dorothy the magical Silver Shoes and a protective kiss from the Good Witch of the North. Seeking a way back to Kansas, Dorothy set off toward the Emerald City along the yellow brick road to consult the Great Oz. Along the journey, she befriended and rescued the Scarecrow, the Tin Woodman, and the Cowardly Lion, who joined her quest. Upon reaching the Emerald City, the Wizard tasked the companions with defeating the Wicked Witch of the West. While forced into servitude in the Witch's castle, Dorothy successfully melted the Wicked Witch with a bucket of water after her Silver Shoe was stolen. Returning to the Emerald City, she discovered the Wizard was a humbug unable to grant her request magically. Eventually, Dorothy traveled south to Glinda the Good Witch, who revealed the secret power of her Silver Shoes, allowing Dorothy to safely tap her heels and return home to Kansas with Toto.

label: History
value: Glinda led her forces to the Emerald City
unit: Glinda led her forces to the Emerald City to capture the wicked witch Mombi and investigate the fate of Princess Ozma. Queen Jinjur attempted to fool Glinda by delivering Jellia Jamb enchanted to look like Mombi, but Glinda quickly detected the deceit, dispelled the illusion, and forced Jellia to confess. Glinda then agreed to terms to enter the city and search for Mombi before sundown. When Mombi transformed into a red rose to avoid detection, Glinda briefly withdrew, but eventually secured Mombi's capture. She brought Mombi before her and interrogated her using a magic pearl that turns black whenever a falsehood is spoken. Through this interrogation, Glinda forced Mombi to reveal that the infant Princess Ozma had been transformed into the boy Tip. Glinda gently comforted Tip and explained that he must resume his true form as Princess Ozma to become the Queen of the Emerald City.

label: History
value: Jack was created by Tip.
unit: After being created by Tip and brought to life, Jack encountered the newly animated Saw-Horse, which accidentally knocked him over onto the moss due to its stiff legs. He suggested to Tip that making ears for the Saw-Horse would allow it to hear commands, and he assisted Tip by holding the horse's head while the ears were inserted. Journeying from the Country of the Gillikins, Jack traveled to the Emerald City to meet its monarch. Upon meeting His Majesty the Scarecrow, Jack initially caused confusion because the Scarecrow mistook his carved smile for laughter, and the two briefly believed they spoke different languages before conversing directly. When invited to sit down, Jack was pushed into an armchair by the Scarecrow and untangled himself. He later accompanied his companions on their journey, hiding his carved smile when the Woggle-Bug made poor puns and worrying about being eaten when Tip expressed hunger. During an attack by angry Jackdaws, the Scarecrow ordered Tip to remove Jack's head so it could be hidden safely beneath straw in a nest.

label: History
value: Mombi lived in the northern Country of the Gillikins in the Land of Oz.
unit: Mombi lived in the northern Country of the Gillikins in the Land of Oz, where she was suspected of practicing magical arts. She acted as guardian to the young boy Tip, whom she made perform various household and field tasks while keeping him under her strict care. Long ago, the Wizard of Oz paid her three visits to entrust her with the baby Princess Ozma; Mombi hid the child by magically transforming her into Tip in exchange for learning the Wizard's magic tricks. Years later, when General Jinjur usurped the throne of the Emerald City, Mombi aided Jinjur and attempted to thwart Glinda the Sorceress through trickery. She used a spell to swap appearances with Jellia Jamb and later transformed herself into a red rose in the palace garden to evade capture. However, Glinda saw through her illusions and forced Jinjur to hand her over. Confronted by Glinda with a lie-detecting pearl and threatened with death, Mombi confessed that she had transformed Princess Ozma into Tip.

However, Glinda saw through her illusions and forced Jinjur to hand her over. Confronted by Glinda with a lie-detecting pearl and threatened with death, Mombi confessed that she had transformed Princess Ozma into Tip.

label: History
value: The Saw-Horse comes to life after Tip applies magical powder.
unit: After Tip applies magical powder, the Saw-Horse comes to life and is amazed to discover his own existence. Lacking ears initially, he fails to hear Tip's commands and accidentally steps on Tip's foot before stumbling into a gopher hole. Tip fits him with ears made of tree bark and teaches him basic commands for travel. Tip then hammers a wooden post into his back to serve as a handhold so Jack Pumpkinhead can safely ride him on their journey to the Emerald City.

value: The Scarecrow is made from a suit of faded blue clothes.
unit: The Scarecrow is made from a suit of faded blue clothes stuffed unevenly with straw, giving his arms and legs a bumpy look. His head is a small sack stuffed with straw, featuring eyes, ears, a nose, and a mouth painted on to form a face. He wears white gloves padded with cotton, and wisps of straw stick out from his coat, neck, and boot-tops. Resting on his head is a heavy golden crown set with jewels that causes his brow to sag into a wrinkled, thoughtful expression.

label: History
value: The Scarecrow sought out the Wizard of Oz
unit: The Scarecrow sought out the Wizard of Oz to receive a brain. During his audience in the Throne Room, the Wizard unfastened his head, emptied the straw, and filled it with a mixture of bran, pins, and needles before restuffing it, leaving the Scarecrow feeling exceptionally wise. Later, while traveling with companions toward the Quadling country, he attempted to lead the group up a rocky hill guarded by the Hammer-Heads. Upon marching forward, he was struck by a shooting flat-topped head and sent tumbling down the hill, prompting Dorothy to call the Winged Monkeys for transport. After ascending the throne as King of the Emerald City, he met Jack Pumpkinhead and mistakenly thought Jack was laughing at him until realizing Jack's carved smile was permanent. Recognizing they spoke different regional tongues, he ordered an interpreter to be brought. During later journeys riding the Saw-Horse with Tip and Jack, his straw body became soaked, but Tip dried and restuffed him back into shape. As they traveled past familiar locations, the Scarecrow reminisced about past adventures, including saving Dorothy from stinging bees and being captured by Winged Monkeys.

label: History
value: After the Wicked Witch of the West was destroyed, Dorothy and the Cowardly Lion set out with the yellow Winkies to find the Tin Woodman.
unit: After the Wicked Witch of the West was destroyed, Dorothy and the Cowardly Lion set out with the yellow Winkies to find the Tin Woodman. They discovered him lying battered and bent on a rocky plain, whereupon Winkie tinsmiths hammered, soldered, and repaired him back to his original form. Upon reunited with his friends, he used his newly fitted gold-handled axe to chop down a tall tree, retrieving the Scarecrow's clothes so their comrade could be re-stuffed. Following the completion of their quest, the Tin Woodman visited the Wizard of Oz in the Emerald City, who placed a heart inside his tin breast, which the Woodman marked with an engraved star. He eventually became the nickel-plated Emperor of the Winkies, ruling from his castle. When his close friend the Scarecrow arrived with Tip and Jack Pumpkinhead seeking refuge after being deposed by General Jinjur's rebels, the Tin Woodman welcomed them warmly and immediately pledged his support and forces to march on the Emerald City and restore the Scarecrow to his throne. During their subsequent perils, he gallantly fought off swarms of attacking Jackdaws using his spinning axe to protect his comrades.

During their subsequent perils, he gallantly fought off swarms of attacking Jackdaws using his spinning axe to protect his comrades.

label: History
value: Tip constructed a wooden figure.
unit: Tip constructed a wooden figure with a carved pumpkin head, named Jack Pumpkinhead, to play a prank on his strict guardian Mombi. After bringing Jack to a bend in the road, Tip repaired a broken arm joint and set him up facing the path. Hiding behind a hedge when Mombi returned, Tip secretly observed her using the magic Powder of Life to bring Jack to life. Later, while journeying to rejoin Jack Pumpkinhead and the Saw-Horse at the Emerald City, Tip ran out of food and encountered General Jinjur by the roadside. Jinjur shared her luncheon with Tip in exchange for carrying her basket, during which Tip learned of her secret Army of Revolt and her plan to overthrow the Scarecrow and seize the throne.

label: History
value: Toto traveled with Dorothy
unit: Toto traveled with Dorothy and her companions through a thick forest on their way toward the Emerald City. When a roaring Lion bounded out and struck the Scarecrow and Tin Woodman, Toto ran barking toward the beast to face it. Dorothy intervened before the Lion could bite him, scolding the Lion and discovering he was a coward. Toto continued traveling alongside Dorothy, eating a bit of everything at supper in a farmhouse and resting beside Dorothy at night while the Lion guarded her door. Upon reaching the green wall surrounding the Emerald City, Toto entered the arched gate with the rest of the group.

label: History
value: The Wicked Witch of the West ruled over the country of the Winkies.
unit: The Wicked Witch of the West ruled over the country of the Winkies, where she enslaved the local population. When Dorothy Gale, the Scarecrow, the Tin Woodman, and the Cowardly Lion ventured into her domain to destroy her, she observed them from her castle using her powerful single eye. She initially sent a pack of forty wolves and later a flock of wild crows to destroy the group, but both attacks failed. After her slaves were scared away by the Lion, she retrieved the Golden Cap from her cupboard to summon the Winged Monkeys for her third and final time. She commanded the Winged Monkeys to destroy the Tin Woodman and the Scarecrow, capture the Lion to be harnessed as a work beast, and bring Dorothy to her castle unharmed. Unable to hurt Dorothy directly due to the protective kiss on the girl's forehead, the Witch made Dorothy her kitchen slave and plotted to obtain her magical Silver Shoes. She managed to trick Dorothy into tripping over an invisible iron bar and stole one of her shoes. In anger, Dorothy threw a bucket of water over the Witch, which unexpectedly caused the Wicked Witch of the West to melt away completely.

unit: The Wicked Witch of the West ruled over the country of the Winkies, where she enslaved the local population. When Dorothy Gale, the Scarecrow, the Tin Woodman, and the Cowardly Lion ventured into her domain to destroy her, she observed them from her castle using her powerful single eye. She initially sent a pack of forty wolves and later a flock of wild crows to destroy the group, but both attacks failed. After her slaves were scared away by the Lion, she retrieved the Golden Cap from her cupboard to summon the Winged Monkeys for her third and final time. She commanded the Winged Monkeys to destroy the Tin Woodman and the Scarecrow, capture the Lion to be harnessed as a work beast, and bring Dorothy to her castle unharmed. Unable to hurt Dorothy directly due to the protective kiss on the girl's forehead, the Witch made Dorothy her kitchen slave and plotted to obtain her magical Silver Shoes. She managed to trick Dorothy into tripping over an invisible iron bar and stole one of her shoes. In anger, Dorothy threw a bucket of water over the Witch, which unexpectedly caused the Wicked Witch of the West to melt away completely.

label: History
value: He is originally from Omaha.
unit: Originally a balloonist and ventriloquist from Omaha, he accidentally arrived in the Land of Oz when his hot-air balloon drifted out of the clouds. Believing him to be a powerful wizard, the inhabitants accepted him as their ruler. He ordered the construction of the Emerald City and mandated that all residents and visitors wear locked green spectacles. In secret, he visited the witch Mombi to learn magic tricks and entrusted her with baby Princess Ozma. To preserve his reputation, he hid behind a screen in his throne room and projected terrifying illusions—such as a giant Head, a lovely Lady, a Beast, and a Ball of Fire—when granting audiences. When Dorothy Gale and her companions arrived seeking his aid, he demanded the destruction of the Wicked Witch of the West as payment. After Dorothy defeated the Witch and exposed him as a fraud, he ingeniously fulfilled his visitors' requests through clever tricks, giving brains to the Scarecrow, a heart to the Tin Woodman, and courage to the Cowardly Lion. He then constructed a hot-air balloon to return to Kansas with Dorothy, but the ropes snapped prematurely, carrying him away alone. Before drifting out of sight into the sky, he officially appointed the Scarecrow to succeed him as ruler of the Emerald City.

label: Appearance
value: The Woggle-Bug is a great, round, buglike creature.
unit: The Woggle-Bug is a great, round, buglike creature fully as tall as the Tin Woodman, standing upright on two slender legs ending in feet with curling toes. His flat body is a glistening dark brown on the back and striped with bands of light brown and white across the front, supported by a long neck and a head with bulging black eyes, a nose ending in a curling antenna, and ears bearing antennae like miniature pigtails. He dresses in a dark-blue swallowtail coat with yellow silk lining and a flower in the buttonhole, a tight white duck vest, fawn-colored plush knickerbockers with gilt knee buckles, and a tall silk hat set jauntily on his head.

label: History
value: The Woggle-Bug began life as a small bug.
unit: The Woggle-Bug began life as a small, ordinary bug crawling under stones in the grass. Driven by curiosity, he entered a country schoolhouse and made a home in a warm hearth nest, where he lived for three years listening to Professor Nowitall's educational discourses. One day, the Professor captured him and projected his image onto a screen using a magnifying glass to display him to the class. Upon bowing politely to the students, the bug startled two girls into falling backward out a window, causing the Professor to rush outside. Taking advantage of the distraction, the bug escaped while retaining his highly magnified state. He later joined Tip, the Scarecrow, the Tin Woodman, Jack Pumpkinhead, and the Saw-Horse on their travels, accompanying them aboard the flying Gump toward the South Country to seek Glinda the Good.
